newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament wants embassies in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament wants embassies in Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel's parliament gave preliminary approval on Wednesday to a bill requiring foreign countries to move their embassies from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem despite international opposition.
Only 13 of the Knesset's 120 members voted on the bill, presented for the first of three readings by lawmaker Rehavam Zeevi of the far-right Moledet party.
The bill, which passed eight to five, aims to force countries to recognise Israel's annexation of Arab East Jerusalem, occupied in the 1967 Middle East war. The bill now goes to committee.
Foreign Minister David Levy, who replied to the motion on behalf of the government, said the bill was "just" but expressed opposition, saying it could not be enforced.

"There is no place in the world where someone will determine where your capital is located," Levy said. "The necessary question is in the reality...We will not be able to enforce it...What kind of sanctions could Israel apply?"
Only two countries -- Costa Rica and El Salvador -- have embassies in Jerusalem. Other countries maintain embassies in Tel Aviv as a sign of their opposition to Israel's annexation of East Jerusalem.

Under a 1993 Israeli-PLO accord that launched limited Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, the future of East Jerusalem is due to be decided during talks on a permanent peace settlement. The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state.
